8afc2c6d5d7c79b9.description: Job description Decima International is a professional services company, providing project management and controls services to clients in the United States and the Middle East. Our mission is to become the premier professional services provider across all industry sectors we are engaged in. To accomplish this, Decima International’s founders established a simple yet powerful formula: Approach each client engagement as a partnership , create an environment that attracts the most talented professionals and allows them to flourish, and regulate growth to maintain excellence in our service standards. We are seeking an experienced Procurement & Contracts Lead to lead the procurement and contracts function on large-scale data center, mission-critical, and infrastructure programs in KSA. The role sits within Decima’s Project Management Consultancy (PMC) teams, acting as the Owner’s onsite representative and leading the full procurement and contract lifecycle for EPC contractors and major project packages on the Client’s behalf. The successful candidate will support procurement and contracting strategy, lead tendering and award activities, manage post-award contract administration, variations, claims, payments, and close-out, and protect the Client’s commercial and contractual position throughout project delivery. RESPONSIBILITIES Support the Client in developing procurement and contracting strategies and lead their implementation across project packages. Develop procurement package plans, tender schedules, bidder lists, and procurement governance processes. Lead contractor and supplier prequalification, capability assessments, RFQs, RFPs, and tendering activities. Prepare and coordinate scopes of work, pricing schedules, contract exhibits, clarification logs, and tender addenda. Lead technical and commercial bid evaluations, including review of bidder qualifications, assumptions, exclusions, pricing, schedules, delivery methodology, and contractual deviations. Prepare bid comparison sheets, evaluation reports, negotiation strategies, and award recommendations for Client approval. Lead tender clarification meetings, bidder interviews, commercial alignment discussions, and negotiations. Coordinate with cost teams to benchmark pricing and validate project budgets. Lead post-award administration of EPC and major project contracts. Review and interpret contractual terms, scope provisions, payment mechanisms, warranties, liabilities, indemnities, and termination provisions. Refer matters requiring formal legal interpretation to the Client’s legal function. Own and maintain contract registers for notices, bonds, guarantees, insurance, payments, variations, claims, and contractual key dates. Prepare procurement and contracts dashboards, claims reports, variation reports, risk reports, and executive updates for the Client’s PMO. Provide guidance to project teams on tender governance, contract interpretation, change management, claims avoidance, and commercial risk. Lead and develop the procurement and contracts team, including contract administrators, procurement engineers, and tendering support staff. Manage team resourcing, package allocation, quality review, and technical development. Coordinate closely with project management, engineering, cost, planning, commercial, commissioning, document control, and Client teams. Escalate matters outside the PMC’s delegated authority to the Project / Site Director for referral to the Client. Maintain confidentiality of contractual, commercial, pricing, and tender information and ensure integrity of the procurement process. Minimum **5 years of experience leading a procurement, contracts, or commercial function**. Strong experience managing the full procurement lifecycle from strategy and tendering through award, administration, and close-out. Strong contractor prequalification and tender management experience. Extensive experience with technical and commercial bid evaluation. 8a0605d1ba4be8fb.description: Job Purpose: The Oracle Fusion Cloud Risk Management Senior Consultant is responsible for leading the implementation, configuration, optimization, and governance of Oracle Fusion Cloud Risk Management solutions. The role works closely with Internal Audit, Finance, Compliance, Security, and business stakeholders to establish effective access governance, segregation of duties (SoD), user access certification, continuous controls monitoring, and financial transaction controls while ensuring compliance with organizational and regulatory requirements. Key Accountabilities: Lead requirements gathering, design workshops, and solution discussions for Oracle Fusion Cloud Risk Management initiatives. Design and implement access governance, segregation of duties (SoD), user access certification, and financial controls frameworks. Configure Oracle Risk Management Cloud modules and capabilities, including: Advanced Access Controls (AAC) Advanced Financial Controls (AFC) Financial Reporting Compliance (FRC) User Access Certification (UAC) Develop and maintain risk libraries, control frameworks, risk models, rule inventories, and SoD matrices. Configure risk detection rules, incidents, remediation workflows, certifications, and governance processes. Assess business roles, privileges, and user access assignments to identify control weaknesses and conflicts. Collaborate with Security, Application, and Business teams to design and implement remediation plans. Configure and optimize continuous monitoring models for high-risk transactions and business controls. Perform rule tuning and false-positive reduction activities while maintaining effective control coverage. Map business processes, risks, controls, and compliance requirements to Oracle Risk Management capabilities. Support control testing, audit readiness, evidence collection, issue management, and remediation tracking. Define integration requirements across Oracle Fusion applications, identity management solutions, and reporting platforms. Lead SIT, UAT, defect management, production readiness reviews, and go-live activities. 8a5a48d0ca1a2473.description: We are seeking an experienced E&I Engineer (Construction Support – CS) with 5–10 years of experience in marine and shipbuilding projects. JOB RESPONSIBILITIES: Provide construction and production support for Electrical and Instrumentation (E&I) installation activities in marine, shipbuilding, and offshore vessel projects. Review, prepare, and revise E&I engineering deliverables, including: Electrical equipment layout and installation drawings Cable routing, cable tray, and cable ladder layouts Cable schedules, termination diagrams, and interconnection drawings Lighting, power distribution, and small power layouts Instrument location and installation drawings Instrument hook-up drawings and installation details Junction box layouts and cable termination details Earthing and bonding layouts Equipment mounting, supports, and installation arrangements 2D production drawings and 3D models for E&I systems Review shop drawings, installation drawings, and production information to identify discrepancies and resolve design-related issues. Provide technical support to shipyard production teams during electrical equipment installation, cable pulling, cable termination, instrument mounting, and system integration activities. Resolve technical queries (TQs), site and production issues, drawing discrepancies, and installation-related engineering problems. Incorporate engineering changes, production feedback, and redline mark-ups into drawings, cable schedules, and 3D models. Coordinate with Hull Structure, Machinery Outfitting, Piping, HVAC, and other engineering disciplines to ensure proper E&I integration and avoid clashes. Review vendor drawings, equipment specifications, cable requirements, and technical documentation to ensure compatibility with vessel arrangements and installation requirements. Verify cable routing, equipment accessibility, installation clearances, maintenance access, and interface requirements before execution. Support constructability reviews and identify potential installation constraints, routing conflicts, and design discrepancies. Ensure E&I installation arrangements comply with project specifications, applicable marine standards, classification society requirements, and shipyard construction procedures. Coordinate with electrical and instrumentation engineers, designers, equipment vendors, and production personnel to ensure timely resolution of technical issues. Support as-built drawing updates and incorporate final production modifications, where required. Ensure construction support deliverables are completed within agreed project schedules and quality requirements. KEY QUALIFICATIONS: Diploma or Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Instrumentation Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or an equivalent engineering discipline. 5–10 years of relevant experience in E&I engineering or construction support within marine, shipbuilding, shipyard, or offshore vessel projects. Hands-on experience in Construction Support (CS), shipyard production support, and E&I drawing modifications. Strong experience in electrical and instrumentation installation layouts, cable routing, equipment positioning, and associated engineering activities. Good understanding of marine electrical systems, power distribution, lighting, earthing, cable management, instrumentation installation, and control system interfaces. Experience preparing and modifying 2D production drawings, cable schedules, installation drawings, and 3D models. Proficiency in marine 3D design software, preferably AVEVA Marine / Hull & Outfitting, or other shipbuilding CAD software accepted by the client. Ability to interpret engineering drawings, electrical schematics, instrument hook-up drawings, cable schedules, vendor documentation, and production mark-ups. Experience resolving technical queries and supporting shipyard production teams during construction and installation activities. Familiarity with marine classification society requirements, applicable IEC standards, shipbuilding standards, and project specifications. Experience coordinating with Hull Structure, Machinery Outfitting, Piping, HVAC, and other engineering disciplines. Understanding of cable routing through bulkheads and decks, equipment mounting arrangements, penetrations, and associated installation interfaces. Experience in new-build shipbuilding projects, offshore vessels, FPSOs, or similar marine engineering projects is preferred. Exposure to international shipyards, marine EPC contractors, or multidisciplinary engineering environments is preferred. Strong technical problem-solving, drawing interpretation, coordination, and communication skills. Ability to work effectively in a project-driven engineering and shipyard production environment. VERTICAL ENGINEERING

8a422ac987cd7379.description: About Tabby Tabby is dedicated to empowering individuals with control over their finances. Work Environment and Benefits Tabby offers a work environment that provides autonomy and responsibility from day one, where the quality of work directly influences career progression. Additionally, Tabby provides Flexi Perks, a monetary benefit that can be used for health and well-being, education and professional development, or travel needs.
